title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from the neighbouring pages): X and Y are smooth projective varieties over k, with dim X = n. A_X and B_X are the Albanese and Picard varieties, and B_Y ≅ A_Y^* by duality. In 2.1 a correspondence Z on X×Y (from the next page, apparently a 1-cycle, so that it acts as H^1(Y) → H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1)) defines a homomorphism u_Z between a Picard variety and an Albanese variety. On the generic point it is given by D ↦ S(Z(D)): transport an algebraically trivial divisor through Z to a degree-0 zero-cycle and sum it in the Albanese.

Corollary 2.2. The dual homomorphism ^t(u_Z): B_Y → A_X equals u(^tZ), the map attached to the transposed correspondence. Concretely, for D algebraically equivalent to 0 on Y with Z(D) defined, S_X(Z(D)) = ^t(u_Z)(D). The margin warns 'attention aux signes éventuels', and the check is to be done cohomologically.

Proposition 2.3 (under the hypotheses of 1.1, where Z is presumably a divisorial correspondence). The marked dual map is v_Z = ^t(u_Z): B_X → B_Y. For D algebraically equivalent to 0 on X, ^tZ(D) = ^t(u_Z)(D). In other words, pulling divisor classes through the transposed correspondence is the dual of the Albanese-to-Picard map. The margin says this should be moved up to section 1. The N.B. proposes using this for another proof of 1.1, via a lemma on homomorphisms of group schemes Pic_{X/k} → Pic_{Y/k}. Verification is to be by 'AQT' (unclear abbreviation).

Proposition 2.4 (finished on the next page). Fix ℓ. Suppose the map induced by the class of Z, H^1(Y,Q_ℓ) → H^{2n-1}(X,Q_ℓ)(n-1), is an isomorphism; this is equivalent to u_Z being an isogeny. Then there is a divisor D with rational coefficients on X×Y whose cohomological action H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) → H^1(Y) is the inverse. D is unique modulo algebraic equivalence ⊗Q and induces u_Z^{-1} in Hom(A_Y,B_X)⊗Q. D can be taken integral iff u_Z is an isomorphism; denominators are controlled by the degree of the isogeny.

Purpose: establish the H^1 case of the Lefschetz-type standard conjecture (algebraicity of the inverse of a correspondence that is an isomorphism on H^1), using the theory of Picard and Albanese varieties.
errors: The source and target of u_Z are written inconsistently across pages (B_X→A_Y on the previous page; v_Z: B_X→B_Y marked on this page). These are notational slips in a draft.
Signs: Grothendieck himself flags possible sign errors twice. The identities hold up to the sign conventions for duality of abelian varieties, but are not fully checked here.
The statement of 2.4 is left unfinished on this page. The conditions 'cond. réd./nécessaire et suffisante...' are partly crossed out and ambiguous.

ideas.what: Dual of the homomorphism induced by a correspondence on Picard/Albanese equals the homomorphism induced by the transposed correspondence (2.2, 2.3)
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of Pic^0/Alb under correspondences; compatibility with duality of abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (theory of correspondences), Lang 'Abelian Varieties' (1959); Matsusaka
ideas.where_published: Classical; used implicitly in Grothendieck 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) and Kleiman's exposé in Dix exposés (1968)

ideas.what: Inverse of a 1-cycle correspondence that is an isomorphism on H^1 is algebraic (a Q-divisor on X×Y); integrality iff u_Z is an isomorphism (2.4)
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture B(X) / A(X) in degree 1 (H^1 case)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1969, standard conjectures) and Kleiman (1968), via Weil/Lang theory of Albanese-Picard
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968/1969), remark that the H^1 case follows from abelian variety theory; Kleiman, Dix exposés 1968

ideas.what: Idea of reproving 1.1 by a lemma on homomorphisms of group schemes Pic_{X/k} → Pic_{Y/k}
ideas.modern_name: Representing homomorphisms of Picard schemes by divisorial correspondences (Hom(Alb_X,Pic^0_Y) ≅ divisorial correspondences mod equivalence)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil, Lang; Grothendieck FGA for Picard schemes
ideas.where_published: FGA (Picard scheme) for the scheme theory; the correspondence theorem is classical

deep.surprise_reason: This is draft work on the H^1/divisorial case of the standard conjectures via Picard and Albanese varieties. That material is classical (Weil, Lang) and the H^1 Lefschetz case is explicitly noted in Grothendieck's and Kleiman's 1968-69 texts. The integrality refinement (integral D iff u_Z is an isomorphism, denominators dividing powers of N) is a nice detail but follows directly from duality theory.
transcription_corrections: In 2.4 the source of cℓ(T(Z)) appears to be H^1(Y,Q_ℓ) (written over X), consistent with the next page; the target is H^{2n-1}(X,Q_ℓ)(n-1).
The phrase after 'soit un isomorphisme' seems to read 'isogénie' / '(cond. néc. et suff.: que u_Z soit une isogénie)' rather than 'cond. réd. de Lefschetz'.
In the N.B. the word read as 'relèvement' is uncertain; it may be 'homomorphisme(s)' ('via un lemme sur les homomorphismes de groupes Pic_{X/k} → Pic_{Y/k}').
In 2.2 'Z(D)' should presumably be '^tZ(D)', since D lives on Y.
